history.idea: Replace random order with a filtered, deduplicated, target-similarity-ranked selection. Steps: (1) Drop exact and near duplicates: build a hash of the whitespace-normalised, lowercased first 500 chars plus the full hash of the first tokenised text, deduplicate docs sharing the same key and keep the first occurrence. (2) Drop junk: docs shorter than 200 chars, or with low vocab complexity (unique-word ratio < 0.5 for tokens, or zlib compression ratio compressed/unc compressed < 0.2), or non-ASCII/non-vestigial-logo-heavy. (3) Fit a word-level TF-IDF (analyzer='char_wb', ngrams=[1,2], max_features=50000, sublinear_tf, on a character-n-gram hash-footer of each doc's first 3000 chars to get a cheap unique-token set estimate) trained on target_sample + docs that pass the cheap threshold, or simply use a setof(counter) over whitespace-normalised first 3000 chars of each target doc vs pool doc key hash, scoring pool doc similarity to those keys. Get plain-text only docs (reject docs with <5% alphabetic/space chars or with web junk markers like 'coupon', 'discount code', 'free shipping'). Also reject word-shuffled artifacts: build the set of word bigrams from target_sample and from each doc's first 1000 chars; mark a doc as damaged if its hit ratio (number of its bigrams in the target bigram set) divided by its bigram count is below half the hit ratio of the target-sample median doc. (4) Count tokens with tiktoken gpt2, per doc. (5) Score each surviving doc as the fraction of its target bigrams; shuffle the score distribution slightly by adding uniform noise scaled to 0.2x the data SD so ranking dominates. Score all 200 target docs and mute them so they do not affect the ranking. Rank the surviving pool docs by score descending. Take docs from the top until the cumulative token count reaches about 1.05 T. If the docs that score above a threshold (e.g. 0.4 x the 5th percentile of target-scored clean docs) are under 0.7 T, still top up with next-best-scoring clean docs rather than repeating. (6) Return the selected indices in seeded random order (CURATE_SEED). If the clean, deduplicated set is smaller than 0.5 T tokens, add the lowest-score docs among kept ones up to 0.5 T, with no other fallbacks.

history.idea:
Keep the dedup, junk and word-shuffle filters, but rewrite the scoring from a word-bigram hit ratio (which cannot see within-document order violations) to a full-order n-gram similarity, and make the selection calibrate to exactly T tokens with a hard fallback to repeated higher-score docs.

(1) Tokenise with tiktoken gpt2. For each doc compute the exact hash of adjacent word trigrams (whitespace-normalised, lowercased, keyed FP16 hash, e.g. hashlib.md5 of ' ' + a + ' ' + b + ' ' + c). Trigrams are large enough to be cheap to hash and strict enough to catch word-shuffled and letter-scrambled text.

(2) Build the trigram set from the 200 target docs. For each pool doc compute h = number of its trigrams in the set divided by its trigram count (0 if shorter than 200 tokens). Also compute m = the same ratio for a replicated copy of the target set; this is the baseline that matches ordering perfectly.

(3) Calibrate the threshold. Sort the target docs by h and take the 5th percentile value t. Students that are clean, intact target-style articles should score about t, while shuffled or generated text should score far below.

(4) Change the damage check. Old: hit ratio < 0.5 x the median target ratio. New: h < 0.4 x t AND the doc holds fewer than 100 unique trigrams. This keeps the clean target-like docs (whose h is near t) and only dropsWikiText-style damaged ones.

(5) Add web-junk markers to the reject list: the doc contains at least 3 of {'coupon','discount code','free shipping','buy now','Order cannes','Get hazard'}. Do not filter on sensible-word fraction anymore, since the real damage is order corruption.

(6) Score every surviving doc as h. Shuffle scores by adding uniform noise with std = 0.1 x the pooled SD so ranking is not machine-determined.

(7) Select. Sort docs by score descending. Accumulate tokens with tiktoken gpt2 (estimate len/4 to cheap start, then re-count with tiktoken once the top picks are chosen; a second pass over the top ~2000 docs costs little and fixes the budget). Keep docs while the cumulative total is below 1.025 T. If the docs with h >= 0.5 t hold at least 0.7 T, keep only those and shuffle the list.

(8) Hard fallback. If the h >= 0.5 t set is smaller than 0.5 T, return only that set, seeded-randomised. If it is smaller than 0.7 T, top it up to 0.7 T with the next-best-scoring clean docs, still without repeats. Only if kept docs total less than T, repeat the kept list; do not bring in unselected pool docs.

(9) Output. Return the selected indices in seeded random order (CURATE_SEED).
history.outcome: dev 1.8378 against 1.9389 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea: Mix a small clean target-style supplement into the selection without repeating the whole list. (1) Keep the current setup: trigram hit ratio h against the target trigram set, threshold t at the 5th percentile of the 200 target docs, junk markers and the damage check h < 0.4 t with fewer than 100 unique trigrams, plus dedup on whitespace-normalised, lowercased first 800 chars hash. (2) Normalise both sets by estimating the target vocabulary fraction, using the 0th, 0.5th and 1st quartiles of the character bigram entropy of the 200 target docs (computed with string.madeusage on the first 2000 chars of each; for each doc in the pool compute the same and let k = (0.5th + 1st quartile) / (0th + 0.5th quartile) of target docs). Change the pool score to h * k, so FakeNewswire docs that use a poorer lexicon are not automatically spared. (3) Same normalisation for the teacher: let each target doc's score be its internal hit ratio times its own quartile ratio, and define the baseline as the average of those normalised internal scores. (4) Calibrate t as the 0.05-quantile of the normalised target scores, still mark damaged as h < 0.4 t with fewer than 100 unique trigrams, and keep the 0.5 t bonus. (5) Fill as before: the h >= 0.5 t clean docs, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, then output in seeded random order. (6) New step: build the set B of the ~3000 most frequent whitespace-token bigrams over target_sample. For each clean doc compute r = bigrams of its first 1500 tokens that are in B divided by its bigram count in the same range; this mostly risks word-shuffled text which the trigrams cannot see. Sort all clean docs by r. Count the clean docs whose normalised h >= 0.5 t and call that set S. Let r5 be the 5th percentile of r among the ~200 target docs. If S has fewer than 0.5 T tokens and its 5th percentile r is at least 0.6 * r5, copy the 15% of pool docs with the lowest r that are not in S, add them to S, shuffle S and rewrite the whole selection as that augmented S, capped at 0.7 T. If the h >= 0.5 t set is under 0.5 T, behave as the present best: return only that set, shuffled and seeded-randomised, no filler. Otherwise leave the present best intact: only if the kept set totals less than T let it repeat in the list according to the rule it already follows, and never draw unselected pool docs. (7) No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.3 T, just return that, seeded-randomised.

history.idea: Keep the current best (experiment 2) intact and add a second, cheap damage pass that決賽 the long docs (>2000 tokens). (1) Build V, the set of whitespace-normalised, lowercased word unigrams from the 200 target docs. For each pool doc compute u = unique unigrams / total unigrams over its first 3000 tokens. (2) Build W, the set of adjacent unigram pairs from the target docs, and for each doc compute p = pairs in W / pairs over the first 2500 tokens, using a sparse counter so the lookup is cheap. (3) Compute the same u and p for the target docs; let m_u and m_p be the 0.025-quantiles of the target unigram and pair ratios. (4) Mark a doc as secondarily damaged if u < 0.3 * m_u or p < 0.3 * m_p, even if its trigram h >= 0.5 * t. Literally shuffled copy-pastes, letter-noised text and blog news with a different topical vocabulary get caught this way; the unigram/pair scores are robust against word-shuffle because within-document adjacency is destroyed. (5) Apply the mark with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass, but also check it only on docs that have at least 100 unique unigrams to avoid noise on short docs. (6) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only: the h >= 0.5 * t set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise exactly as now. (7) No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised. (8) Log the numbers (final counts, tokens and h distribution) and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final output order.

history.idea: Add a second damage pass aimed at WikiText-style documents (target is FakeNewswire) that the trigram test cannot see, because their word order is intact. (1) Build B, the set of whitespace-normalised, lowercased word bigrams over the 200 target docs. (2) For every pool doc compute r = bigrams of its first 3000 tokens that are in B divided by its bigram count in the same range. (3) Compute the same r for the target docs; let r0 be the 0th percentile (minimum) of the target r values. A doc is secondarily damaged if r < 0.5 * r0, even if its trigram h >= 0.5 * t; shuffle text keeps trigrams while destroying bigrams. (4) Apply the mark with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass, and only on docs with at least 100 unique tokens. (5) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only, exactly as now: the h >= 0.5 * t set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise as adaptation 2. (6) Log the numbers (final counts, tokens and h distribution) and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final output order. No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised.

history.idea: Add a second damage pass aimed at word-shuffled wiki-style documents, which the trigram test cannot see because enough trigrams still match. (1) Build B, the exact set of adjacent word bigrams over the 200 target docs, lowercase and whitespace-normalised. (2) For every pool doc compute r = bigrams of its first 3000 tokens that are in B divided by its bigram count in the same range, using a sparse dict so the lookup is O(1). (3) Compute the same r for the target docs; let r0 be the 0th percentile (minimum) of the target r values. R is internally calibrated: clean target text has r near 1.0, and shuffled text has r well below that. (4) Reuse the alphabetic check from now, but make it literal: any char with ord > 122 or non-ASCII, which is not used now, is junk; anything below 50% alphabetic/space chars is junk, for the first 3000 tokens and grouped in 500-token windows so ratios are stable on short docs. Also use already-deduplicated docs only. (5) A doc is secondarily damaged if r < 0.6 * r0, or if any of its adjacent windows has alphabetic/space rate below 0.55. The r0 bound is loose enough to spare intact-format documents with low-level damage, and documented by the word-shuffle pool examples. Apply the mark with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass, and only on docs with at least 150 unique tokens. (6) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only, exactly as now: the h >= 0.5 * t set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise as experiment 2. (7) Log the numbers (final counts, tokens and r distribution) and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final output order. No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised.

history.idea:
Keep the current best intact and add a second damage pass aimed at copy-and-paste, template or boilerplate documents that make perfect sense but do not belong in the target domain, such as WikiText plain-text articles with 'Posted by admin in', 'Add to Favourites' and 'Read more >>' headlines, but which score as clean because their vocabulary matches the target. This was never tested, only dropped with the existing web junk markers.

(1) Build K, the set of whitespace-normalised, lowercased adjacent word bigrams from the 200 target docs.

(2) Define filler markers as the set {'Posted by admin', 'Add to Favourites', 'Read more >>', 'Home | About', 'Login | Register', 'Cart (0 items)', 'When you'.

(3) For each doc compute s = number of its K bigrams that occur in the set of target bigrams plus filler-marker bigrams, divided by its bigram count over the first 2500 tokens, with a sparse dict lookup.

(4) Compute the same s for the target docs; let s0 be the 0th percentile (minimum) of the target s values. Normalised, clean target docs have s near 1.0; copy-and-paste boilerplate docs have s far below, even though their trigram hit ratio is high. Let s0.5 be the 0.5th percentile of the target s values.

(5) A doc is secondarily damaged if s < 0.7 * s0 and it holds at least 100 unique tokens, or if it holds at least 3 filler markers. Apply the mark with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass.

(6) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only, exactly as now: the h >= 0.5 * t set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise as experiment 2.

(7) Log the numbers (final counts, tokens and s distribution) and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final output order. No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised.

history.idea:
Keep the current best (experiment 2) intact and add a second damage pass aimed at letter-noised and character-corrupted text, which the trigram test cannot see because it hashes already-tokenised whitespace words, so a char-level substitution such as 'A' -> '4', 'a' -> '@' or ' ' -> '.' leaves each word intact.

(1) To build the baseline on the 200 target docs: lowercase and whitespace-split the first 2000 tokens of each and count the unigram frequency of each token. Build D, the set of tokens that have at least 2 occurrences in at least one target doc.

(2) For every pool doc compute c = number of its tokens that fall in D, divided by the number of tokens that have at least 2 occurrences in the doc itself. Compute the same c for the target docs; let c0 be the 0th percentile (minimum) of the target c values. Clean text gives c near 1.0; letter-noised text gives c far below, because half the characters are wrong and their tokens no longer match D.

(3) Reuse the alphabetic check from experiment 4 as a hard baseline: any doc with fewer than 80% alphabetic/space chars is junk.

(4) A doc is secondarily damaged if c < 0.6 * c0 and it holds at least 500 tokens. Apply the mark with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass, and only on docs with at least 500 tokens so the threshold is not noisy.

(5) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only, exactly as now: the h >= 0.5 * t set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise as experiment 2. (6) Log the numbers (final counts, tokens and c distribution) and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final output order. No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised.  Guess: target text is plain ASCII with space punctuation, so the same check is leave it alone with at least 50% alpha/space chars, even over quivering windows. -> dev

history.idea: Keep the current best (experiment 2) and add a second damage pass aimed at the letter-noisedWikiText documents that the trigram test cannot see. Since the pool examples show a pattern ('It and Africa ; @-@ known' / 'First . identified Two by John Gray was' / 'Crowd of 82  , 000' where ' , ' is written ' , '), the damage is within each whitespace word, so the set D of tokens with at least 2 occurrences in the target makes no sense. Instead: (1) Lowercase and whitespace-split the first 2000 tokens of each target doc and build F, the set of adjacent character bigrams of alphabetic characters, e.g. ' ' + ' b' + ',', 'f ,', ' . i', 'or ,' - count them as a frozenset of tuples or as hash of ' ' + b1 + ' ' + b2 + ' '. Apply the same construction to each pool doc. (2) For each doc compute d = number of its adjacent alpha-character bigrams that are in the set of target bigrams plus the space punctuation bigrams (e.g. ' , ,' ' . ,') divided by its number of adjacent alphabetic character bigrams, over the full text or the first 2500 tokens, whichever is shorter. Do F, d for the target docs and let d0 be the 0th percentile (minimum). Clean text gives d near 1.0; letter-noised text gives d far below, because half the characters are wrong. (3) Compute the same d under two shifts, with a small amount of junk tolerance exactly as the pool shows: build D1 = the target bigrams plus the 300 most frequent bigrams over the target docs and the filler bigrams such as 'or ' and ', ' and ' .' and ' @', and compute d1 with D1, and D2 = the target bigrams plus the 1500 most frequent bigrams, and compute d2. Let med be the median of the target d values. (4) A doc is secondarily damaged if any of d0 * 0.5, d1 * 0.7, d2 * 0.7 is at most 0.6 * med, or if its mean of the three is at most 0.4 * med, and it holds at least 300 tokens. The shifted scores let the test stand against off-by-one and space-punctuation damage such as ' 2000 .' ' 2012 , ' . (5) Apply the mark with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass, and only on docs with at least 300 tokens. (6) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only, exactly as now: the h >= 0.5 * t set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise as experiment 2. (7) Log the numbers and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final order. No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised. Guess: the target is clean ASCII so leave it alone with at least 50% alpha/space chars.

history.idea:
Keep experiment 2 intact and add a second damage pass aimed at SCI/TeX-style documents (with '= Title =' and 'Word , ' bigrams) that score as clean on target bigrams because the target is also a large Newswire format.

(1) Build X, the set of whitespace-normalised, lowercased adjacent character 3-grams of alphabetic characters over the first 2500 tokens of each target doc, e.g. ' b ,' ' , a', 'er .' - hash them as bytes for speed.

(2) For each pool doc compute x = number of its adjacent alpha-3-grams that are in X divided by its number of adjacent alpha-3-grams, falling back to adjacent bigrams if the 3-gram count is below half the 0.5th-percentile 3-gram count of the target docs. Build the same x for the target docs and let x0 be the 0th percentile (minimum).

(3) Compute x under two shifts as in experiment 9: X1 = X plus the 300 most frequent character 3-grams over the target; X2 = X plus the 600 most frequent character 3-grams. Let med be the median of the target x values.

(4) A doc is secondarily damaged if any of x0 * 0.5, x1 * 0.7, x2 * 0.7 is at most 0.5 * med, or if its mean of the three is at most 0.35 * med, and it holds at least 200 tokens.

(5) Apply the mark with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass.

(6) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only, exactly as now: the h >= 0.5 * t set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise as experiment 2. (7) Log the numbers and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final order. No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised. Guess: the fixed-size target gives a tight 0th percentile, so setting the cut at 0.5 * med leaves space to catch fallible, intact-format articles that copy the '= Title =' style.

history.idea:
Add a second damage pass aimed at the word-shuffled and letter-scrambled documents shown in the pool prefixes, which the full-order trigram test cannot see because a large fraction of adjacent word trigrams still match. The first pass (experiment 2) leaves this damage on the selection.

(1) Build G, the set of whitespace-normalised, lowercased word trigrams over the 200 target docs.

(2) For each pool doc compute r = number of its adjacent word trigrams that are in G divided by its number of adjacent word trigrams, over the first 3000 tokens, with a sparse dict lookup. Compute the same r for the target docs and let r0 be the 0th percentile (minimum).

(3) Build the set M of adjacent character 3-grams over the target docs, lowercased, e.g. ' b ,' ' , a'. For each pool doc, count how many of its adjacent character 3-grams over the first 3000 tokens are in M, and divide by the number of adjacent character 3-grams. Do the same for the target docs and let m0 be the 0th percentile.

(4) A doc is secondarily damaged if its word-trigram rate r is below 0.6 * r0 and it holds at least 200 unique trigrams, or if its character-3-gram rate m is below 0.5 * m0 and it holds at least 300 characters. Both checks apply with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass, and only on docs that pass the first pass.

(5) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only, exactly as now: the h >= 0.5 * t set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise as experiment 2. (6) Log the numbers (final counts, tokens and r/m distribution) and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final order. No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised. Guess: there are at most a few thousand such docs in the pool compared with T, so a final overkill pass whose effect is visible here will be decisive.

history.idea: Keep the current best (experiment 2) intact and add one more check specifically for the 'word-bigram shuffled' docs that still make sense word-for-word with a target-like lexicon, so they have h near t, pass the 0.4 t damage test, and are not caught by the existing filler-marker list. (1) Build H, the frozenset of adjacent whitespace-token bigrams over the 200 target docs, lowercased. For each pool doc compute q = number of its adjacent bigrams that are in H divided by its number of adjacent bigrams, over the first 2500 tokens, with a sparse dict lookup. Do the same for the target docs and let q0 be the 0th percentile (minimum). Clean target text gives q near 1.0; a doc whose words are shuffled within sentences gives q far below. (2) Make the target hit rate internally calibrated by量少: build also the set R, the 3000 most frequent adjacent bigrams over the target docs, and compute q1 with H plus R. Let med be the median of the target q values. Environment-varying damage such as ' , ' / ', ' or off-by-one tokens lets the same doc survive both the plain and the shifted plain checks, so keep one plain check as well. (3) A doc is secondarily damaged if q is below 0.75 * q0 and it holds at least 150 unique bigrams, or if q1 is below 0.6 * med and it holds at least 100 unique bigrams. Both apply with no hysteresis and independently of the first pass, and only on docs that pass the first pass. Add a final guard: if a doc's set of unique tokens has fewer than 5000 characters in total, mark it damaged, which catches memoised boilerplate that is reused exactly across docs. (4) Retrain selection on the surviving docs only, exactly as now: the q1 >= 0.6 * med set, shuffled, up to 0.7 T, then next-best clean docs up to 1.025 T, with the same 0.7 T hard fallback and the same repeat-or-cycle rule; otherwise as experiment 2. (5) Log the numbers (final counts, tokens and q/q1 distribution) and use the existing CURATE_SEED for the final order. No other fallbacks; if the surviving clean set is under 0.5 T, return only that, seeded-randomised.
